collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager discovers their family has kept a hard secret about the past: ask about it, or leave it buried.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Clearing out (subject.his/her) grandmother's hut, (subject) found a carved board with names on it that nobody in the family ever mentions, and a scratched-out mark beside them. (subject) has asked (friend), the eldest of the family, what it means. (friend)'s face closed like a door. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) asks again, a week later, gently. (friend) tells only a little: something hard happened to the family a long time ago, in the old days, that nobody wanted to remember. Some names were lost with it. (friend) does not say more. (subject) does not ask more. (subject.He/she) hangs the board in the family hut.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) puts the board away and does not ask. But (subject.he/she) cannot stop thinking about it. Years later, at the end of (friend.his/her) life, (friend) asks for the board, and holds it, and says the names out loud, one by one. Then (friend.he/she) gives it back.
